children: EU antitrust investigators opened a full-scale investigation into Austrian furniture retailer XXXLutz's proposed acquisition of German peer Porta on Monday, saying the deal may significantly impact competition in several EU countries, a move which could require XXXLutz to offer remedies to address their concerns.

XXXLutz, whose brands include XXXLutz, Mömax, Roller, Braun, Home24 and Möbelix and also sells electronics and appliances in addition to furniture and household goods  announced the deal in January 2025.

The European Commission, which is the EU competition enforcer, said its preliminary review of the deal signalled some concerns especially in the market for the retail sale of furniture in discount stores.

"Within these markets, the transaction may remove important competitive constraints between the companies, as they are among the few players in Germany, Czechia and Slovakia operating furniture retail store networks offering the full range of furniture," the Commission said in a statement.

It said manufacturers and suppliers in Germany, the Czech Republic, Slovakia and Poland may also be impacted by the deal due to XXXLutz's purchasing association GIGA International which gives the company significant purchasing power.
It set a February 25 deadline for its decision.

XXXLutz found itself in EU antitrust regulators' crosshairs in July this year which opened a separate investigation into whether it had implemented the deal without first securing their approval.  The company could face a hefty fine as much as 10% of its global annual turnover if found guilty of jumping the gun.
